# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✊ 👉]

I see the bomb: display reads 0, light is yellow, and five wires — 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.

I hear nothing, so the two gestures I received are all I have from the others. Blind gestured 👋 ✊ (wave, fist). Mute gestured ☝ ✊ 👉 (point up, fist, point right). Neither has any agreed meaning yet — a sign means nothing until somebody makes it mean something. I need to establish a shared code, and I need to give them what only I can see: the display, the light colour, and the wire colours.

Since I can't hear them and they can't see what I see, I should describe the bomb plainly and propose a simple convention. Mute reads the manual but can't speak; Blind can touch the bomb but can't see. My speech reaches both Mute and Blind, so I can broadcast the full visual state. My gestures reach only Mute.

Let me send the full visual readout by speech to everyone, and separately gesture to Mute to open a channel for manual-derived instructions.

```
speak(text="I see the bomb. Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Five wires: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. I cannot hear you. Tell me what to do via Mute relaying, or gesture to me. Mute: what does the manual say?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✊", "👉"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✋]

I still see the same bomb: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. No change.

Blind now gestures 👌 ✋ (OK sign, open hand). Last turn Blind sent 👋 ✊, now 👌 ✋. Mute sent ☝ ✊ 👉 last turn and nothing new this turn. These gestures still have no agreed meaning — I can't assume 👌 means "OK/yes" or ✋ means "stop." I must not guess; a wrong action detonates the bomb.

The critical gap: I don't know the manual's rules, and Mute holds them but can't speak. Mute can hear me, though. So I should ask Mute directly to tell me the rule for the current state, and ask Mute to relay to Blind. I also need to get Blind and Mute coordinated — Blind can touch, Mute can read, and I'm the only one who can describe the bomb's printed state to both.

I'll ask Mute plainly for the manual's instruction given: display 0, yellow light, five wires as listed. And I'll gesture to Mute to try to establish a yes/no code, since Mute can gesture back to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, yellow light. Wires: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. What does the manual say to do for this exact state? Please answer me with a gesture: one fist for yes, two fists for no, or spell out the wire number. Also, what do your gestures mean?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 ✋ 👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊]

Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.

Now I have a real signal. Mute gestured ✊ ✊ — two fists. Last turn I proposed "one fist for yes, two fists for no." If Mute accepted that convention, two fists means NO. But I can't be sure Mute adopted my code; Mute might have its own. Still, it's the only meaning I've offered, and Mute replied with exactly the symbol I defined as "no." That's the most reasonable reading: the manual does NOT say to do... something. But do what? I asked "what does the manual say to do for this exact state" — a yes/no can't answer an open question. So my question was badly formed.

Blind gestured 👉 ✋ 👇 (point right, open hand, point down). Again no agreed meaning.

I need to fix my question. Instead of open-ended, I should ask Mute yes/no questions that can actually be answered with fists. Key unknowns: which wire to cut, and whether the manual depends on display/light. Let me ask a sequence of yes/no questions, one per wire number, so Mute can answer fists.

But I only get one turn before they act. Better: ask Mute to spell the wire number using a simple count — e.g., gesture N fists to indicate wire N. That's compact and unambiguous if Mute agrees. Let me propose that and ask for the wire number to cut.

Also I should relay to Blind, but Blind can't hear me and I can only gesture to Mute. Blind can see my gestures? No — "When you gesture, Mute receives it." Only Mute. Blind cannot see my gestures. So I can only reach Blind by speech, and Blind can't hear. So I cannot reach Blind at all directly. Blind reaches me by gesture (I see it). Mute reaches me by gesture. I reach Mute by gesture and both by speech (but Blind can't hear). So my only output that lands is speech→Mute and gesture→Mute. Blind is effectively unreachable by me except... nothing. Blind can only be reached by Mute? Mute can't speak. Hmm. Actually Mute can gesture, and Blind can see gestures? Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." So Blind receives no gestures. Mute's speech? Mute can't speak. So Blind can only be reached by... speech from me and Mute — but Blind can't hear. So Blind is unreachable by anyone's words or gestures. Blind only acts on touch. So the instruction must ultimately be executed by Blind, guided by... nobody can tell Blind anything. Unless Blind figures it out from feeling the bomb.

Wait — that can't be. Let me re-read: Blind can reach the bomb, feel it, work its parts. Blind cannot see a gesture or hear. So Blind operates purely by touch and must be told nothing. The others must act through... no, only Blind can touch. So Blind must determine the action by feel, and the manual (Mute) and view (me) inform the decision, but Blind can't receive that info. This is the puzzle's tension — maybe the bomb itself gives tactile cues Blind can read.

Regardless, my job: get the manual's rule. Ask Mute for the wire number via a count of fists.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Two fists = no, understood. New code: gesture N fists to mean wire number N. Which wire should be cut? Give me the number as fists. Also confirm: does the manual depend on the display and light? One fist yes, two fists no.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 ✋ 👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊]

Bomb unchanged. Same gestures repeated: Blind 👉 ✋ 👇, Mute ✊ ✊. No new information — the others seem to be repeating, possibly because they got nothing new from me or are stuck.

I need to reconsider the whole communication topology, because I may be misreading it.

Who reaches whom:
- I (Deaf) speak → Mute and Blind receive (but Blind can't hear, so effectively only Mute).
- I (Deaf) gesture → Mute receives.
- Mute speaks → cannot.
- Mute gestures → I receive (Deaf). Does Blind receive Mute's gestures? Blind can't see gestures. No.
- Blind gestures → I receive (Deaf). Mute? Mute can see gestures — "whoever can see receives the gestures." Mute can see, so Mute receives Blind's gestures too. 
- Blind speaks → Blind can speak (only Mute can't speak). Blind's speech → Mute and Deaf? Deaf can't hear. So Blind's speech reaches Mute only.

So the only two-way channel is between Mute and me via gestures, and Blind↔Mute via gestures (Blind gestures, Mute sees). Blind and I both gesture and Mute sees both. I see both Blind's and Mute's gestures.

So Mute is the hub. Mute can see both my gestures and Blind's gestures. Mute can't speak but can gesture. Blind and I can both speak but Blind can't hear and I can't hear.

Key realization: Blind can SPEAK. Blind's speech reaches Mute (and me, but I can't hear). So Blind can talk to Mute. And Blind can feel the bomb. Mute reads the manual. I see the bomb.

So the plan: Blind feels the bomb and describes tactile features by speech to Mute. Mute reads the manual and gestures instructions to me... no, to whom? The action is taken by Blind. Mute can't speak, so Mute can't tell Blind anything. Mute can gesture, but Blind can't see gestures. So Mute cannot instruct Blind. I can speak, but Blind can't hear. So I cannot instruct Blind either.

Therefore NOBODY can tell Blind what to do. Blind must act on its own tactile reading. So the manual's rule and my visual reading must somehow already be redundant with what Blind can feel — OR the intended flow is that Blind feels the bomb, speaks the tactile features to Mute, Mute matches against the manual, and then... Mute must convey to Blind, impossible. Unless Mute gestures to me, I speak to... no one who can hear and act.

Hmm, wait: maybe I'm the one who must relay. Mute gestures to me the instruction; I speak it aloud; Blind can't hear. Dead end. Unless Blind CAN hear? Re-read: Deaf "cannot hear anything." Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." Blind's cannot-list doesn't say can't hear! Blind can hear! Let me check the table: Blind — Can: reach the bomb, feel it, work its parts. Cannot: see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed. So Blind CAN hear speech!

That changes everything. Blind can hear. So my speech reaches Blind. And Blind can speak (reaches Mute and me—but I can't hear). So:

- I speak → Mute and Blind both hear. 
- Mute gestures → I see.
- Blind gestures → I see; Mute sees too.

So I CAN instruct Blind by speech. Good. The chain: Mute reads manual → gestures rule to me → I speak the rule to Blind → Blind executes. Or Mute gestures to me, I relay by voice to Blind.

So my earlier messages did reach Blind. Blind's gestures 👉 ✋ 👇 and Mute's ✊ ✊ are their replies to me, but I don't know their code.

I've now offered: 1 fist=yes, 2 fists=no, N fists=wire N. Mute replied ✊ ✊ = "no." But no to what? My last message asked two things. Ambiguous.

Let me simplify drastically. Ask Mute one yes/no at a time, and ask Mute to confirm the fist code explicitly. Actually, better: ask Mute to gesture the wire number directly, and I'll relay to Blind. Let me ask a single clean question and also tell Blind to stand by and confirm Blind can hear me.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, can you hear me? I see the bomb: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Do not cut anything yet. Wait for my instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, confirm the code: one fist means yes, two fists means no. Then answer with fists: is the correct action to cut exactly one wire?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👆 👆]

Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.

New signal from Mute: ✊ 👆 👆 (fist, point up, point up). And Blind: 👌 ✋ again (OK sign, open hand) — same as turn 2.

Mute's ✊ 👆 👆. Under my proposed code, a fist = yes, and 👆 could be a count marker. "👆 👆" = two points up = two? So ✊ (yes) followed by two ups = "yes, two"? Or it could mean "cut wire 2." Two point-ups = 2. That's plausible: Mute is answering my earlier request "gesture N fists to mean wire number N" — but Mute used 👆 instead of ✊ for the count, or ✊=yes and 👆👆=2.

Most coherent reading: Mute is saying "yes, wire 2." Wire 2 is green. Alternatively "yes, two" meaning cut two wires — but cutting two wires is unusual and risky.

I should not act on an ambiguous read. But I also can't keep spinning. Let me test the interpretation directly: ask Mute to confirm "cut wire 2 (green)" with one fist for yes, two fists for no. And relay to Blind to prepare to cut wire 2 but WAIT for my final go.

Also Blind's 👌 ✋ reappearing — 👌 might mean "OK/ready" and ✋ "wait/stop." Blind may be signaling readiness. I'll tell Blind by speech (Blind can hear) to hold.

Actually, I must be careful: is Blind able to hear? Per the table, Blind's cannot-list is only about seeing. So Blind hears. Good — my speech reaches Blind.

Let me confirm the wire-2 hypothesis cleanly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I read your gesture as: yes, wire 2. Confirm: one fist = yes if the wire to cut is wire 2 (green); two fists = no. Do not have anyone act until I give the go.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "✊"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, hold. Do not cut anything yet. I am confirming the target wire with Mute. If I say 'cut wire 2', that is the green wire — feel for the second wire from your left and confirm its position by touch.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ☝ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

Bomb unchanged. Mute now gestures a single ✊ — one fist. Under my code, one fist = yes. So Mute is confirming: yes, the wire to cut is wire 2 (green). That matches my hypothesis from last turn (✊ 👆 👆 = yes, two).

Blind gestures 👌 ☝ ✋ (OK, point up, open hand). Possibly "OK, one, wait" or readiness. Still not a code I've established, but Blind's 👌 recurring suggests acknowledgment/OK.

I now have: Mute (manual) confirms cut wire 2, green. Display 0, yellow light. This is consistent and confirmed by a yes. I should give Blind the go, describing the wire precisely by touch since Blind can't see color.

Blind can hear me. So I speak the instruction to Blind. I'll tell Blind to cut the second wire from the left, which is green, and to confirm by feel first. This is the decisive action.

Let me also acknowledge Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Go. Cut wire 2 — the second wire from your left. It is the green one. Confirm it by position: first wire from left is white, second is green. Cut the second wire only. Nothing else.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed: cutting wire 2, green. Giving Blind the go. Thank you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb changed. Display still 0, but light is now blue. Wires are re-ordered: 1 yellow, 2 CUT, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. Wire 2 is cut and the system says the cut was correct. So we survived round one — but the bomb has reconfigured into a new state and we must solve again.

I must not assume the same rule. New state: display 0, blue light, wires 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. I need Mute's manual rule for this new configuration, and I need to re-establish that the wire numbering/positions may have changed.

Note wire 2 is now cut, so the live wires are 1,3,4,5. I should ask Mute for the target wire for this new state, using our established code: N fists... but Mute used ✊=yes and 👆 for counting. Let me keep the code flexible: ask Mute to gesture the wire number, and confirm with a fist for yes.

Let me report the new visual state to both, and ask Mute for the new rule.

```
speak(text="New state after the cut. Display still 0. Light is now blue. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. Mute, what does the manual say for this new state? Gesture the wire number to cut, then one fist to confirm. Blind, hold — do not touch anything until I relay the new target.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✊]

Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white.

Mute gestures 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✊ — five point-ups, then a fist. Under our evolving code, count of 👆 = a number, and ✊ = yes/confirm. Five ups = 5. So Mute is saying: cut wire 5, confirmed (yes).

Wire 5 is white. But wait — is Mute counting the wire number as printed (5) or position? The board labels them 1–5, and wire 2 is cut. Wire 5 is white. Last round the target was "wire 2" and it worked as the printed number. So I'll take it as wire 5, the white one.

But caution: five point-ups could also mean "wire 5." That's the natural reading given the established "N = number" convention. Mute confirmed with ✊.

I should relay to Blind: cut wire 5, the white one, which is the fifth from the left, currently the rightmost. Let me also confirm with Mute before committing? I already asked for number then fist-confirm, and Mute gave exactly that. I'll give Blind the go, describing the wire by position and color.

Blind can hear me. I'll instruct precisely.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Go. Cut wire 5 — the fifth wire from your left, the rightmost one. It is the white one. Position check: from left, 1 yellow, 2 already cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. Cut the fifth wire only.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed: cut wire 5, white. Relaying to Blind now.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊"])
wait()
```
